transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! How are you feeling after your cataract surgery? Do you have any questions about your surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi there! I'm doing okay, but I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can start with light gardening, such as brisk walking, gardening, light jogging, and gentle cycling, about 1 week after surgery. Just remember to be gentle and avoid any strenuous activities for a month. Also, don't forget to wear protective eyewear when gardening to keep your eyes safe.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Great, that sounds good to me. Thank you! My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can start using preservative-free eye drops, which can help with dryness, four times daily. If you were already using eye drops before your surgery, you can continue using them unless you were told otherwise. You can also get more eye drops from your GP if you need them.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for clarifying that. I'm also noticing that I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Yes, it's normal to be a bit sensitive to light after cataract surgery. Wearing sunglasses when you're outside can help. If the sensitivity is severe or if your eye is also red and painful, we may need to assess it further. But if it's just mild and things seem brighter than usual, the sunglasses should help.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That's reassuring to hear, thank you. One last question: should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's common to have some blurriness in the first week after surgery, but it should improve quickly and settle down over time. If your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure it's okay.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I appreciate the explanation. That's all the questions I had. Thank you for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome! It was my pleasure to help. Do you feel like all your questions about your cataract surgery recovery have been answered?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I feel much better now. Thank you for addressing my concerns!

verdict.label: pass
